```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("R/00_setup_packages.R")
```

## 0. Check your setup

Run this first. If something fails later, paste this output when you ask for help.

```{r env}
report_environment()
pkg_ok <- ensure_packages("ggplot2")   # use upgrade_old = TRUE right after upgrading R
has_ggplot <- isTRUE(pkg_ok[["ggplot2"]])
```

## 1. Data frames

```{r dataframes}
portfolio <- data.frame(
  ticker = c("ALPHA", "BETA", "GAMMA"),
  sector = c("Tech", "Energy", "Utilities"),
  weight = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2)
)
str(portfolio)
portfolio[portfolio$weight > 0.25, ]          # filter rows
portfolio[order(-portfolio$weight), ]         # sort

prices <- read.csv("data/prices.csv")
prices$date <- as.Date(prices$date)
head(prices)
summary(prices)
```

## 2. Simple returns

$r_t = \frac{P_t}{P_{t-1}} - 1$, computed separately for each ticker.

```{r returns}
prices <- prices[order(prices$ticker, prices$date), ]
prices$ret <- ave(prices$close, prices$ticker,
                  FUN = function(p) c(NA, p[-1] / p[-length(p)] - 1))
head(prices[prices$ticker == "BETA", ], 5)
```

## 3. Summary statistics

```{r stats}
stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(prices, prices$ticker), function(d) {
  r <- na.omit(d$ret)
  data.frame(ticker = d$ticker[1],
             mean_daily = mean(r), sd_daily = sd(r),
             ann_vol = sd(r) * sqrt(252),
             total_return = d$close[nrow(d)] / d$close[1] - 1)
}))
knitr::kable(stats, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 4. Bar chart (ggplot2, with a base-R fallback)

```{r bar, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
if (has_ggplot) {
  ggplot(stats, aes(x = ticker, y = total_return * 100, fill = total_return > 0)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#2E7D32", `FALSE` = "#C62828")) +
    labs(title = "Total return over the sample", x = NULL, y = "Return (%)") +
    theme_minimal()
} else {
  barplot(stats$total_return * 100, names.arg = stats$ticker,
          col = ifelse(stats$total_return > 0, "#2E7D32", "#C62828"),
          main = "Total return over the sample (base R)", ylab = "Return (%)")
  abline(h = 0)
}
```

Count-style bar chart, the classic first ggplot2 exercise:

```{r bar-count, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3}
up_days <- data.frame(ticker = prices$ticker, direction = ifelse(prices$ret > 0, "up", "down"))
up_days <- up_days[!is.na(up_days$direction), ]
if (has_ggplot) {
  ggplot(up_days, aes(x = ticker, fill = direction)) +
    geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
    labs(title = "Up vs down days", y = "Days") + theme_minimal()
} else {
  barplot(table(up_days$direction, up_days$ticker), beside = TRUE, legend.text = TRUE,
          main = "Up vs down days (base R)", ylab = "Days")
}
```
